headline: Non-renewable resources don't replenish—once used, they're gone for good on human timescales
universal_truth: Some things don't come back; recognize what's finite and treat it accordingly
fun_facts: It takes millions of years to form oil—we're using millions of years of accumulation per year
Helium is escaping Earth's atmosphere—once released, it's lost to space forever
Rare earth elements essential for electronics are finite—we're depleting concentrated deposits
discussion_questions: What in your life is non-renewable—can't be replaced once spent?
How do you treat finite resources differently than renewable ones?
What irreversible decisions have you made?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Oil formed over 300 million years from ancient organisms. We're burning through centuries of accumulation every few minutes. When it's gone, it's gone—at least for another few hundred million years. Some things don't come back.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often treat finite resources as if they're unlimited. This creates inevitable depletion. What's the right approach to non-renewables?

options.text: Use non-renewables strategically—for high-value purposes where no renewable alternative exists; treat them as precious because they are; plan for their eventual absence
options.response: Yes. Non-renewables should fund transition to renewables, not be wasted on trivial uses. Every drop of oil used is a drop unavailable for future needs. Finite resources deserve finite thinking.
Hopefully, but banking on future solutions while depleting current resources is risky...

q1.title: Timescale Mismatch
q1.script: Non-renewable doesn't mean never—it means not on relevant timescales. Oil will form again, but not for millions of years. For practical purposes, once depleted, it's gone.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Timescale Mismatch"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Depletion Curve
q2.script: Non-renewables follow depletion curves. Easy deposits get used first. Later extraction costs more, requires more energy, yields less. Running out isn't sudden—it's gradual decline.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Non-Renewables
q3.script: You have non-renewables too: time is the ultimate one. Youth doesn't come back. Some opportunities close permanently. Some relationships, once broken, can't be restored. Treat finite things as finite.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Some things don't come back. Recognize what's finite and treat it accordingly. Not everything can be renewed.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 272. Tomorrow, we'll explore power from the sun—solar energy. Until then, identify what in your life is truly non-renewable.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Finite Resource Audit - What Won't Come Back?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify non-renewable resources and use them wisely
growTrack.activity: What in your life is truly non-renewable—time, specific opportunities, irreplaceable relationships, unique moments? How are you spending these finite resources? Are you using them for worthy purposes or wasting them on trivial things?
